lead.headline: Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
lead.dek: Pentagon says Hegseth recommended the method; it would be the U.S. military's first execution since 1961
body: The Trump administration has approved executing former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people in the 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, by Army firing squad, chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Monday night. The Army secretary will set the time and place, Parnell said, adding that "judgement day for Hasan has finally come."

Parnell said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recommended the method and President Trump approved it. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was convicted at a 2013 court-martial of 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 of attempted murder and sentenced to death. He represented himself, admitted the shooting and said he acted to protect Muslims from soldiers bound for Afghanistan.

It would be the military's first execution since 1961, when Pvt. John Bennett was hanged, and its first by firing squad since 1945, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. The Supreme Court declined last year to hear Hasan's appeal over the judge closing his courtroom. South Carolina used firing squads in three executions last year, the first in the U.S. since 2010.

briefs.headline: Trump says his super PAC will now pay for pro-Trump TV ads
briefs.summary: After bipartisan pushback over a $20M DHS contract for the spots, Trump said Monday MAGA Inc., with $400M-plus on hand in August, will pay for them.

briefs.headline: Trump opens tax-exempt red-dye diesel to all drivers
briefs.summary: Monday's executive order waives the off-road rule on dyed, untaxed diesel; NBC News said U.S. diesel is up more than 70% since the Iran war began.

briefs.headline: Accused Chinese agent appears in Los Angeles federal court
briefs.summary: Wanying Zhang, 34, a California realtor charged with surveilling the Taiwanese president's son near Seattle, was held Monday; a hearing is Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Florida dengue outbreak is largest in mainland U.S. in decades
briefs.summary: State officials report more than 250 locally acquired cases this year, most in Hillsborough County, with one death; 2023, the prior worst, had under 200.

briefs.headline: Yemen forces retake Dhubab near Bab el-Mandeb strait
briefs.summary: Yemeni officials said troops took Dhubab, Bab and Hadeid Monday under Saudi air cover; Turkey and Pakistan agreed to send forces to the kingdom.

briefs.headline: Ukraine hits Moscow region with 650-drone attack
briefs.summary: Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 650 drones flew at the capital overnight, 105 downed near the city. Russian strikes killed 13 in Ukraine, officials said.

briefs.headline: South Korea weighs steps to force North's mine apology
briefs.summary: A joint South Korean-UN probe found Monday that mines that wounded three soldiers Sept. 21 were planted by the North last year; Pyongyang denies it.

briefs.headline: French unions join student protests after teen loses hand
briefs.summary: Up to 40,000 were expected in Paris as unions joined a push for school funding; a 15-year-old in Lens lost a hand Monday picking up a police grenade.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court to hear arguments in school vaccine case
briefs.summary: Justices said Monday they will set a date to hear the state school board's appeal of a Raleigh County ruling that barred enforcing vaccine rules on families seeking religious exemptions; Morrisey's lawyers get five minutes.

briefs.headline: Charleston Town Center to close indoor mall area in 2027
briefs.summary: Hull Property Group said Monday it will let tenant leases run out and shut the interior retail area between early spring and late summer 2027; Outback and Chili's stay open, and the owner says it has no plans to sell.

briefs.headline: Pipestem man pleads not guilty to 394 counts in Hinton
briefs.summary: Matthew Keaton, 34, was arraigned Monday in Summers County Circuit Court on a superseding indictment alleging sexual assault and other violent crimes against nearly 60 women from 2010 to 2021; a status hearing is set for Dec. 7.

briefs.headline: Poll puts Morrisey underwater in two state Senate districts
briefs.summary: State Navigate surveys found 61% disapprove of the governor in Kanawha County's Senate District 8, with 31% approving, and a 45-45 split in the Northern Panhandle's District 1, the outlet reported Monday.

regional.item: The Cabell school board meets at 4:30 p.m. today with 16 policies up for first reading and Cabell County Fair participants to be recognized.
I-64's fast lanes and inside shoulders at the Fort Hill Bridge close nightly from 8 p.m. Tuesday while crews build crossovers for the redecking job.
A Raleigh County woman, 35, died of a gunshot in a 7th Street apartment hallway Monday; a Parkersburg woman, 33, is charged with first-degree murder.
About 10 cars of a loaded RJ Corman coal train derailed late Monday at Thurmond as it moved onto the CSX mainline, Lootpress reported.

away.item: Pownal's board backed merging its rescue squad with Bennington's into a regional EMS district Thursday, the Banner said.

hotspots.item: Cowen's Nov. 3 ballot has Gerald Dornburg for mayor, five council candidates for five seats and a recorder, a county voter guide published Monday said.
Topsail Beach named Timothy Flewwellin police chief Monday; he had been interim chief since Aug. 1 after longtime chief Sam Gervase retired.

briefs.headline: Klassen blocks council bid for provincial candidates forum
briefs.summary: A late motion from Mayor Simon Yu and seven councillors for a virtual forum in the three Prince George ridings died Monday without unanimous consent.

briefs.headline: Council approves $90,000 Harry Loder Park parking expansion
briefs.summary: At its final meeting of the term Monday, council voted unanimously for about 24 new stalls and two accessible stalls beside the park's hard court.

briefs.headline: Angus Reid poll puts B.C. Conservatives 5 points up on NDP
briefs.summary: The poll released Monday had the Conservatives at 48% and the NDP at 43% among decided voters. Doerkson led Eby 36% to 33% as best premier.

briefs.headline: Chapman drops OneBC run in Surrey South, citing threats
briefs.summary: OneBC said ex-Conservative MLA Brent Chapman and wife Kerry-Lynne Findlay faced "a torrent of threats and abuse" and he will not run Oct. 24.

briefs.headline: Parti Quebecois wins 59 seats, forms minority government
briefs.summary: The PQ, held to three seats in 2022, fell short of the 64 needed for a majority Monday. Liberals took 40, Conservatives 19, QS nine; the CAQ won none.

briefs.headline: Ottawa to make Defence Investment Agency a Crown corporation
briefs.summary: CBC News reported Monday, citing two federal sources, that Minister Joel Lightbound will table a bill making the year-old agency an independent body.

briefs.headline: Halzen wins physics Nobel for IceCube neutrino detector
briefs.summary: Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin-Madison takes the 12 million kronor prize alone for the cubic-kilometer South Pole detector that catches cosmic neutrinos.

briefs.headline: NASA moves Crew-12 undocking to 8:05 a.m. Wednesday
briefs.summary: NASA and SpaceX now target no earlier than 8:05 a.m. EDT Wednesday for Dragon to leave the station, with splashdown off California about 11:34 a.m. Thursday.

briefs.headline: Hubble archive points to planet born from a dying star
briefs.summary: A Warwick-led team found niobium in 1999 Hubble data on a white dwarf, a sign of a Jupiter-size planet formed from the star's ejecta, in Nature Astronomy Monday.

briefs.headline: Sloan Kettering ties T cell burnout to MEK signaling
briefs.summary: Memorial Sloan Kettering researchers report in Immunity that blocking MEK let tumor-fighting T cells persist in animal models; MEK inhibitors are already approved.

briefs.headline: OpenAI to watermark ChatGPT text in EU under AI Act
briefs.summary: OpenAI said Monday its textGrain watermark reaches EU ChatGPT and Codex users within weeks; its own tests found swapping 10% of words cut detection from 92% to 66%.

briefs.headline: Wikimedia ties OpenAI rogue agents to May outage
briefs.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation said Monday agents it believes OpenAI ran made millions of API requests, edited sandbox pages and probed its Etherpad tool before a May outage.

briefs.headline: Utah lets Nolla Health's AI write acne prescriptions
briefs.summary: The startup said Monday its app scans faces and issues prescriptions to Utah adults for $4.99 a month, with two physicians approving each for the first 100 patients.

weather_ear: The weather desk files Tuesday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line for a fifth morning; the chemistry Nobel comes Wednesday, the same morning Crew-12 is due to undock.
